Incident Name: Delaware Bay Container Vessel Collision & Fuel Oil Spill
4 MapSketch include sketch showing the t: North-oriented map of a 6.0-mile radius centered at Delaware Bay Shipping Channel Buoy 14 near Lewes, Delaware. At Buoy 14, M/V Atlantic Voyager collided with a bulk carrier and breached port fuel tank #3. A 3.5-mile heavy-oil sheen extends East-Southeast toward Cape Henlopen. Prime Hook National Wildlife Refuge 4.0 miles Northwest and Cape Henlopen salt marshes 2.5 miles South are threatened. A USCG HC-144 observed a 300-yard-wide IFO 380 slick drifting on the flood tide. The slick moves East-Southeast at 2.2 knots under West-Northwest winds at 14 knots. Two miles of Cape Henlopen beach and dunes are impacted. Show Staging Area Echo at Lewes Ferry Terminal, the Sector Delaware Bay Command Post, a 1,000-yard Maritime Safety Zone, Boom Sites 1 through 3, and wildlife protection zones.
5 Situation Summary and Health and Safet: At 22:15 on 06/29/2026, M/V Atlantic Voyager collided with M/V Pacific Trader, breaching port fuel tank #3 and spilling approximately 25,000 gallons of IFO 380 before internal transfer stopped the discharge. Hazards include benzene and H2S vapors, dermal toxicity, oily-surface slips, nighttime over-water operations, drowning, and wildlife exposure. Enforce a 1,000-yard Maritime Safety Zone; require Level C PPE, PFDs, and half-mask organic-vapor respirators; continuously monitor H2S and VOCs aboard response vessels; enforce work-rest hydration cycles; and operate mobile vessel decontamination at Lewes Pier.
7 Current and Planned Objectives: Secure the maritime perimeter and stabilize the vessel by 01:00; protect Cape Henlopen salt-marsh inlets with boom by 04:00; begin offshore skimming by 05:30; activate wildlife rescue and rehabilitation by 06:00; and establish Unified Command by 02:00.
ActionsRow1: USCG Station Lewes response boats 45601 and 45602 responded and established the maritime safety zone.
ActionsRow2: Captain P. Hayes established Local Command and requested mobilization of an MSRC oil-spill response vessel.
ActionsRow3: The M/V Atlantic Voyager crew completed internal fuel transfer and halted discharge from fuel tank #3.
ActionsRow4: The USCG HC-144 overflight completed infrared oil-slick mapping.
ActionsRow5: The Delaware DNREC team arrived at the Lewes Command Post and Unified Command was established.
ActionsRow6: MSRC Response Vessel Delaware Responder deploys 2,500 feet of ocean containment boom at Buoy 14.
ActionsRow7: Deploy sorbent diversion boom at Cape Henlopen Inlet, Boom Site 2.
ActionsRow8: Tri-State Bird Rescue begins a shoreline wildlife search along Cape Henlopen beaches.
